NOT SOURCE OF TRUTH for skill bodies' — it never says it covers only the kit half, never names SKILLS-local.md, and never hints that 13 local skills and 4 further kit skills exist outside its 10-row table. verdict.verdict_reason: Quote verified spanning docs/SKILLS-local.md:68-69 (finding cites 69). Checked each half of 'Both headers now say so'. SKILLS-local.md's own header (lines 5-14) does state scope explicitly: 'Two halves with different owners… whose generated index is [`SKILLS.md`]… The roster immediately below spans **both** halves'. docs/SKILLS.md's header block (lines 3-8) does not: it says only 'Generated by substrate-kit. The table below renders FROM the kit's `SKILLS` list… **NOT SOURCE OF TRUTH** for skill bodies' — it never names SKILLS-local.md and gives no signal another half exists. `grep -c 'SKILLS-local' docs/SKILLS.md` = 2, both at lines 44 and 48, inside the '⚠ skills --build does NOT install' bullet, ~40 lines down. Tried to refute via SKILLS.md line 12-13 ('every recurring action that has a defined, kit-shipped procedure'), which is a partial scope signal — but that string is verbatim kit template text (present in bootstrap.py's `SKILLS-index.md.tmpl`), so it is not the fix the paragraph claims to have shipped, and it is preceded by 'The registered skill set for fleet-manager', which reads as complete.

Low blast radius: the boot file separately points at docs/SKILLS-local.md as 'the installed roster with one line per skill', so a booted session still reaches the full list. The defect is the false self-report that the fix landed on both files.

claim: The harvester that produces docs/planning/idea-backlog.md finds every session-card 💡 idea, so the backlog is the machine-built candidate list every groom can start from (per the script's own PROVENANCE header).
quote: BULLET_RE = re.compile(r"^- (?:\*\*)?" + MARKER)
why_wrong: BULLET_RE only matches a 💡 at the start of a top-level list item ('- 💡' / '- **💡'). Across .sessions/, 116 cards use the '## …💡' HEADING form and only 57 use the bullet form the regex accepts. The docstring discloses that 'Inline 💡 mentions mid-prose are NOT harvested' but never says the heading form — the majority convention — is also invisible, so the generated '4 ungroomed' figure reads as a measurement of the corpus when it is a measurement of one minority formatting style.

verdict.verdict_reason: Quote exact at line 66: `BULLET_RE = re.compile(r"^- (?:\*\*)?" + MARKER)`. harvest_blocks() at lines 90-105 uses BULLET_RE as its sole entry condition, so the regex is genuinely the whole harvest gate. I tried to refute via the docstring disclosure — lines 39-41 do say 'Scans .sessions/*.md for top-level bullets carrying the 💡 marker (`- 💡 …` / `- **💡 …`) ... Inline 💡 mentions mid-prose are NOT harvested' — but that does not save it, because docs/planning/README.md:18 advertises the output as an index of 'every `.sessions/*.md` card 💡 idea' and the generated file's own summary line reads as a corpus measurement. A Python enumeration over all 345 files confirms the counts exactly as claimed: bullet-form 57, heading-form 116 (115 of which have no bullet form at all), and 170 further cards whose only line-initial marker is a paragraph start — 285 cards carrying a structured 💡 the regex never sees, against 57 it does. Both named example cards check out: .sessions/2026-07-10-order-003-007-review-queue.md:51 is '💡 **Session idea:** wire the N=50 auto-append rule…' and .sessions/2026-07-10-order-013-games-conformed.md:64 is '💡 **Session idea** (dedup-grepped `docs/`)…'. Running the generator today yields '57 idea block(s) across 345 card(s) · 4 ungroomed'.
verdict.commands_run: sed -n '1,54p' scripts/gen_idea_backlog.py; sed -n '55,110p' scripts/gen_idea_backlog.py; python3 inline script enumerating BULLET_RE/heading/paragraph-start marker forms across .sessions/*.md; grep -n '💡' .sessions/2026-07-10-order-003-007-review-queue.md .sessions/2026-07-10-order-013-games-conformed.md; python3 scripts/gen_idea_backlog.py --stdout | sed -n '1,14p'; sed -n '18p' docs/planning/README.md
verdict.correction: The docstring is less silent than the finding allows — lines 39-41 do say 'top-level bullets' and give the two accepted forms, which by exclusion covers the heading case. The defect is better stated as a mismatch between the script's honest narrow contract and the two surfaces that advertise it as complete: docs/planning/README.md:18 ('every `.sessions/*.md` card 💡 idea', 'grooming passes start here') and the generated file's own '57 idea block(s) across 345 card(s)' summary line. why_wrong: docs/SKILLS.md's table renders only 10 rows — `scope-backlog-item`, `chase-references`, `prep-owner-steps` and `rationalize` are absent from it, though all four are in the vendored kit's SKILLS list (bootstrap.py:14516ff), all four are installed under .claude/skills/, and both seat-digest.md and docs/SKILLS-local.md list them. So the two kit-generated renders of the same list disagree, and the one that self-describes as the full index ('Check this index before improvising a workflow', 'regenerates ... so it cannot hand-drift') is the incomplete one — a session consulting SKILLS.md would conclude four installed skills do not exist.
evidence_cmd: for s in chase-references prep-owner-steps rationalize scope-backlog-item; do printf '%s SKILLS.md=%s seat-digest=%s installed=%s\n' "$s" "$(grep -c "\`$s\`" docs/SKILLS.md)" "$(grep -c "\`$s\`" docs/seat-digest.md)" "$([ -d .claude/skills/$s ] && echo yes || echo no)"; done; sed -n '14516,14670p' bootstrap.py | grep -oP '^\s+"name":\s+"\K[a-z-]+' | wc -l

verdict.verdict_reason: Quote exact at line 36. Enumerated rather than eyeballed: docs/SKILLS.md's table is lines 22-31 = 10 rows; seat-digest.md lines 21-34 = 14 entries; I parsed the vendored kit's SKILLS list out of bootstrap.py and got 14 names ['session-close','upgrade-distribution','release','intake','scope-backlog-item','chase-references','prep-owner-steps','rationalize','quality-gate','review','repo-health','deep-research','question','analysis']; `ls .substrate/skills/` = the same 14; all four disputed skills are present under .claude/skills/. So the two kit renders of one list genuinely disagree, and SKILLS.md — the one whose header claims it "regenerates at adopt/upgrade, so it cannot hand-drift" and tells sessions to "Check this index before improvising a workflow" — is the short one. Its own body at lines 49-55 supplies the mechanism: a touched planted doc is classified `consumer-edited` and apply_doc_improvements() skips it, so the drift is permanent, not pending.
verdict.correction: Overstated: only TWO of the four (`rationalize`, `scope-backlog-item`) are absent from SKILLS.md entirely. `chase-references` and `prep-owner-steps` DO appear, at lines 87-100 under "## Fleet seed skills — pointer (not kit-shipped yet)", which wrongly says their bodies live in superbot — stale rather than missing. The finding's backticked grep returned 0 for all four because that section writes them bold, not backticked. Also already-known: docs/SKILLS-local.md § "What this roster fixed" (MEASURED 2026-08-08) documents both defects and declares itself the true list until a regen clears them, and .claude/CLAUDE.md routes sessions to SKILLS-local.md for the installed roster — so a boot-path-following session is not misled.
verdict.commands_run: for s in chase-references prep-owner-steps rationalize scope-backlog-item; do grep -c "\`$s\`" docs/SKILLS.md docs/seat-digest.md; [ -d .claude/skills/$s ]; done; cat -n docs/SKILLS.md | head -50; grep -n -i 'chase-references|prep-owner-steps|rationalize|scope-backlog|seed skills' docs/SKILLS.md; sed -n '50,120p' docs/SKILLS.md; python3 (regex parse of SKILLS: list[dict] in bootstrap.py) -> 14 names; ls .claude/skills/ .substrate/skills/; sed -n '1,110p' docs/SKILLS-local.md

quote: > **BINDING — auto-append rule (ORDER 003, 2026-07-10, program-review §5.2):**
why_wrong: Both halves describe apparatus that no longer exists and one half contradicts the live boot file. There is no manager, no failsafe-wake batch and no 12-repo active fleet (program closed 2026-07-21; roster.md shows 0 LIVE rows). The 'no PR ever waits for review before landing' policy is contradicted by .claude/CLAUDE.md:218 — '**Never merge a PR you have asked Codex to review before it answers**' — and by docs/workflow-pr-merge-policy.md, which makes a Codex-clean review of the exact head SHA a precondition for merging any .github/workflows PR. The append rule is also unenforced: `python3 bootstrap.py check --strict` fans out through scripts/preflight.py and never touches this file, and the session-close skill does not mention it. evidence_cmd: sed -n '3,20p' docs/review-queue.md; grep -n 'Codex to review before it answers' .claude/CLAUDE.md; grep -rn 'review-queue' .claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md scripts/preflight.py docs/current-state.md .claude/CLAUDE.md; grep -c 'LIVE' docs/roster.md

verdict.verdict_reason: Quote verified verbatim at line 11 by `sed -n '1,25p' docs/review-queue.md`; line 3 is `> **Status:** `living-ledger`` and line 7 is `> **no PR ever waits for review before landing.**`. `grep -ni 'historical|era note|retired|seat-era|Status:' docs/review-queue.md` returns NO era banner — the only 'retired'/'Historical' hits are line 40 (a retired wall), 58 (a parenthetical about pre-2026-07-11 tiers), 108/115/153 (individual row verdicts). I tried to refute on reachability and failed: `docs/CAPABILITIES.md:1457-1458` (a live doc) names it as the PRIMARY drain path, and `docs/PROJECT-CLOSEOUT.md:158,182` (boot-read-path entry 5) cites `docs/review-queue.md:8` — so a session does reach it. `docs/workflow-pr-merge-policy.md:18` confirms 'Codex reviewed the current head commit' as a merge precondition.
verdict.commands_run: sed -n '1,25p' docs/review-queue.md; grep -ni 'historical\|era note\|retired\|seat-era\|Status:' docs/review-queue.md; grep -n 'Codex to review before it answers' .claude/CLAUDE.md; grep -rn 'review-queue' .claude/skills/session-close/SKILL.md scripts/preflight.py docs/current-state.md .claude/CLAUDE.md; grep -c 'LIVE' docs/roster.md; grep -n 'review-queue' docs/CAPABILITIES.md docs/PROJECT-CLOSEOUT.md docs/playbook.md; grep -n 'Codex' docs/workflow-pr-merge-policy.md
